$comment: The wallets this demo stack knows about. DEV ONLY.
Every seed below is public: the first three are the well-known Midnight CFG_PRESET=dev
genesis seeds, the fourth is the seed Lace uses for its own testing, and the demo-*,
aa-* and shielded-night-* ones are placeholders invented for this repo. They control
value only on a throwaway local `undeployed` chain. Never reuse any of them anywhere
else.
ONE FACADE PER SEED. Two long-lived wallet facades on one seed against one node force
each other's connection down, silently. That is why every service that holds a wallet
open has its own: genesis-1 = funding faucet + offer-files kernel, genesis-2 = batcher,
genesis-3 = AA deploy, aac0… = AA console relay, 7a4e… = AA taker, 5e5e… = shielded-night
deployer, d00d… = shielded-night verify driver, 0ffe… = the offer poster. `lace-test` is
deliberately held by no
service at all, so a browser can import it at any time.
Addresses were produced with `midnight-node-toolkit:2.0.0-rc.4 show-address --network
undeployed --seed <seed>` and are stable for a given seed + network id — they do not
depend on the chain, so they stay valid across a ./down.sh -v reset.
funding = 'genesis'      : the CFG_PRESET=dev genesis already funds this wallet AND
registers its DUST address. Nothing to run. Asserted by
scripts/verify-wallets.sh.
funding = 'fund-script'  : empty until scripts/fund-wallet.sh (or the `fund` compose
service) is run for it.
funding = 'compose-one-shot' : funded by a compose one-shot belonging to its own profile,
not by scripts/fund-wallet.sh. Today that is the offer poster:
compose/poster.yml's `poster-fund` sends it NIGHT before the
poster starts, and the POSTER registers its own DUST address (a
second registrant for a value the service already owns would make
'the poster could not register' unreportable). Deliberately NOT
selected by fund-in-container.sh or verify-wallets.sh: this
wallet's lifecycle belongs to the profile, not to the fund script.
funding = 'mnemonic'     : same as 'fund-script' (empty until funded), but the wallet is
reachable from a BIP-39 mnemonic, so it can be imported into
Lace by hand. See the 'mnemonic' and 'derivation' fields and
tools/mnemonic-wallets/.
Wallets that carry a 'mnemonic' field have a 128-hex 'seed' that is NOT an arbitrary
secret: it is the BIP-39 master seed of that mnemonic (empty passphrase). That is what
makes the toolkit and Lace agree on the same wallet — verified both ways by
tools/mnemonic-wallets/cross-check.sh. Re-derive and assert with:
./tools/mnemonic-wallets/derive.sh --check wallets/wallets.json

$comment: Midnight's own canonical test wallet, reachable from three directions that all agree:
* midnight-node's Earthfile genesis-seeds block lists this 64-byte seed as
'wallet-seed-3' with the comment 'wallet-seed-3 is the wallet Lace uses for testing';
* @midnight-ntwrk/testkit-js@5.0.0-beta.6 defines TEST_MNEMONIC as exactly the
mnemonic below (23x 'abandon' + 'diesel') and WalletSeeds.testWallet() builds from it;
* the BIP-39 master seed of that mnemonic (empty passphrase) IS this seed, byte for byte.
So the seed is a BIP-39 master seed, which is why it is 64 bytes rather than 32.
Verified prefunded on CFG_PRESET=dev: 250,000,000 NIGHT + DUST registered at genesis.
wallets.mnemonic: abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon diesel

wallets.name: shielded-night-deployer
wallets.role: deploys the ShieldedNight wrapper contract ONCE per stack (profile `shielded-night`)
$comment: A DEDICATED seed, not one of the three genesis wallets. genesis-1 is the funding
faucet and the offer-files kernel's MIDNIGHT_WALLET_SEED, genesis-2 is the batcher's
and genesis-3 is the AA deploy wallet's; a second wallet facade on any of them forces
the first one's connection down with nothing naming the cause (spec FR-009).
shielded-night's own scripts fall back to genesis-1 when MN_SEED is unset, so the
deploy entrypoint REFUSES that seed outright rather than trusting the environment.
Funded at bring-up by the `shielded-night-fund` one-shot in compose/shielded-night.yml
(the same toolkit lane scripts/fund-wallet.sh uses), which SKIPS a wallet that already
holds NIGHT and a spendable DUST UTXO — so repeated ./up.sh runs cost seconds.
It is a ONE-SHOT facade: the container deploys, publishes contract.json and exits.

wallets.name: shielded-night-driver
$comment: DISTINCT FROM THE DEPLOYER by requirement (spec FR-011): the round trip must be driven
by a wallet the deployer is not also holding open. The verify entrypoint refuses both
the deployer's seed and genesis-1.
The 1.x sibling repository (midnight-1-offers) has no funding lane and therefore borrows
the genesis-funded `lace-test` wallet for this role — project 00007 question Q6. This
stack has scripts/fund-wallet.sh and the toolkit, so it provisions a seed nothing else
will ever hold open, and the Lace/Moth hand test can use `lace-test` at the same time
as ./verify.sh without the two colliding.
Funded at bring-up by the same `shielded-night-fund` one-shot as the deployer.

wallets.name: offer-poster
wallets.role: the offer poster's wallet (profile `poster`): mints one coin and posts one offer per interval
$comment: DEDICATED, and it must stay dedicated: the poster refuses to start (exit 78) if this seed
equals MIDNIGHT_WALLET_SEED / MIDNIGHT_GENESIS_SEED, BATCHER_WALLET_SEED, SOLVER_SEED,
MAKER_SEED / MAKER_OFFER_SEED or TAKER_SEED — two wallet facades on one seed against one
Midnight node force each other's connection down. `scripts/verify-poster.sh --static`
asserts that offline against every seed declared in this file, in compose/ and in
.env.example.
Funded by compose/poster.yml's `poster-fund` one-shot with 4 x 5_000_000_000_000 stars of
unshielded NIGHT — several LARGE UTXOs rather than one, because DUST is generated per
UTXO and the poster pays for a mint AND an offer every interval out of its own dust.
